message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will install Python dependencies, run tests and lint with a single version of Python
# For more information see: https://help.github.com/actions/language-and-framework-guides/using-python-with-github-actions

name: CI tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master ]

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Set up Python 3.7
      uses: actions/setup-python@v2
      with:
        python-version: 3.7
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('requirements.txt') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
        pip install .
        python setup.py install 
    - name: Test with pytest
      run: |
        pytest",
  "rationale": "The workflow installs Python dependencies from requirements.txt on every run with no dependency cache. The repository has a requirements.txt with heavy dependencies (tensorflow, numpy, pandas, scipy, etc.), so repeated pip fetching is measurable. Evidence pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE supports caching dependency downloads with modest measured benefit, and the experiment batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2 measured adding a pip cache to a Python test workflow. Preconditions are met: dependency fetching repeats each run and requirements.txt serves as the cache input key. No contraindications apply: no equivalent cache exists, and pip cache content is not mutable/untrusted in a way that affects test outcomes. The change is minimal—one cache step inserted before dependency installation—and preserves all original build and test steps, permissions, and triggers.",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
